maya_cs: FYI customer ACME reported their quantized endpoint (open-gtp-3b 4-bit w/ calibration) is slower than the fp16 variant after yesterday's rollout. Ticket #8342.
maya_cs: p95 jumped from ~210ms to ~480ms, errors still low but user sees timeouts in their UI :grimacing:
kim_oncall: ack, can you paste the exact model key + config they used? batch size, seq len distribution?
maya_cs: model: redwood/open-gtp-3b-4bit-calib:v2, runtime config: batching=auto, max_batch_tokens=4096, kv_cache=enabled, warmup=false. Customer says typical seq len 128, tail up to 512.
ravi_runtime: thanks. initial thought: calibration changed scale params and pushed select_kernel path to slower fallback (per-token kernel mismatch). sharing profiler snippet.
ravi_runtime: ```
$ ri-profiler --endpoint acme/endpoint-3b4b --samples 50
avg_token_latency: 3.2ms
kv_fetch: 0.8ms
attn_kernel (4bit_fp): 4.6ms  <-- dominates
fallback_count: 23/50
``` 
lucas_perf: that attn_kernel number looks ~2x expected. On similar workloads our 4-bit attn should be ~2.0-2.5ms. Did calibration enable per-layer fp32 slow path?
ravi_runtime: checked the rollout diff: we toggled per-layer scaling refinement to improve quality. It inadvertently enabled the "slow_scale" path when per-tensor variance > threshold.
kim_oncall: any quick repro steps we can run in staging to validate? Customer offered a sample payload.
maya_cs: posted sample payload in ticket: includes two long prompt prefixes (~40 tokens each) repeated; might trigger KV fragmentation.
ravi_runtime: repro command I ran:
```
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $STG" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood/open-gtp-3b-4bit-calib:v2","input":"<ACME_SAMPLE>","max_tokens":120}'
```
I see the same 2.1x p95 regression in staging when sequence >256 and prefix is repeated.
lucas_perf: hypothesis: repeated prefixes + kv_cache reuse is causing more frequent kv cache restores and krook kernel path that doesn't have int4 fused attention. Need trace of kernel selection per step.
ravi_runtime: added trace flag and got sequence of kernel ids: [int4_fast, int4_fast, int4_fallback, int4_fallback, int4_fallback, int4_fallback, int4_fast, ...]
maya_cs: customer impact note: they see UI stuttering when p95 >400ms, asking for ETA on fix.
kim_oncall: mitigation options: 1) roll back to fp16 (easy, perf known) 2) force int8/4bit to use alternate kernel (if available) 3) tweak calibration thresholds to avoid slow_scale path. Which is fastest?
ravi_runtime: sequence:
- Immediate: pin customer to fp16 model variant for urgent relief (cs can issue migration guide)
- Short-term (1-2 days): push config change to disable slow_scale path for calibrated builds (non-invasive)
- Medium (1-2 weeks): implement an optimizer to detect kv fragmentation and prefer fast kernels; add unit perf tests for repeated prefix patterns.
lucas_perf: also recommend adding a perf regression alert that looks at kernel fallback ratio >10%.
kim_oncall: agreed. I'll open an internal change request to pin config for affected customers and schedule patch.
maya_cs: I'll propose this customer comms: "We're rolling you back to the fp16 variant temporarily while we patch the calibration flow. Expect <24h for rollback; we'll follow up with postmortem." thoughts?
ravi_runtime: sounds good. add note about "no model quality regression expected during rollback" and link to ticket.
maya_cs: will do. @deploy-bot can you create canary job for the calibration toggle in staging?
deploy-bot: Created deploy job ci/quant-calib-toggle-staging #422 :white_check_mark:
kim_oncall: next steps assigned:
- maya_cs: notify customer + coordinate rollback to fp16
- ravi_runtime: prepare config patch to disable slow_scale and smoke test in staging
- lucas_perf: add kernel-fallback metric to perf dashboard
- kim_oncall: monitor rollback and revert if signs of instability
maya_cs: pinging customer now. keeping thread updated. :thumbsup:
